 Aaron Gordon amassed 15 points (3-of-10 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), 11 rebounds, three assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Pelicans.
 Ejected in the fourth quarter of Monday’s loss to the Warriors, Gordon was available for all 48 minutes on Wednesday. The double-double was his first of the season, and the 15 points were one more than his total in Denver’s last two games. Gordon has been close to a top-100 player so far, and it isn’t unrealistic to expect him to maintain that production. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Aaron Gordon was ejected from Monday’s game against the Warriors with 8:34 remaining in the fourth quarter. 
 Gordon was given two technical fouls in quick succession after arguing a call, ending his night with 8:34 left in the fourth quarter. He finished with seven points (2-of-10 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and one steal. Marvin Bagley III replaced Gordon in the lineup after he was ejected. 
 Aaron Gordon 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #32 
 Aaron Gordon tallied 20 points (6-of-9 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, one assist, two steals, one block and three three-pointers in Thursday’s loss to the Thunder. 
 A notoriously poor perimeter shooter for most of his NBA career, Gordon has worked hard in recent years to change that. A 41 percent three-point shooter over his last two seasons, the Nuggets forward hit 3-of-4 from distance on Thursday. By comparison, the other starters shot a combined 3-of-15 from beyond the arc against the Thunder. No one should expect Gordon to challenge Stephen Curry, but his perimeter shot is no longer a liability. 
 Aaron Gordon 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #32 
 Aaron Gordon finished Sunday’s exhibition against the Bulls with 25 points (9-of-12 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), six rebounds and three three-pointers. 
 While Gordon finished the 2025-26 season with increased averages in points, rebounds and three-pointers, injuries limited him to 36 regular-season games. As a result, fantasy managers didn’t reap as many rewards from his improvement as they would have liked. Gordon’s perimeter shooting has improved, with the veteran forward making 41.3 percent of his attempts over the last two seasons. AG shot 3-of-4 from deep on Sunday, and while no one expects him to shoot 75 percent consistently, his improved shooting raises his ceiling. 
 Aaron Gordon 
 DEN 
 Forward 
 #32 
 NBA insider Marc Stein reports that teams have registered interest in trading for Nuggets forward Aaron Gordon. 
 Despite being limited to 87 regular-season games over the last two seasons due to injuries. Gordon is a popular player heading into the offseason. According to Stein, the athletic forward is the veteran Nuggets player who has drawn the most trade interest from opposing teams. However, he also reported that if Denver were to make a move, they would prefer to find a trade partner for Christian Braun rather than for Gordon or Jamal Murray. Making a move would likely make it easier for the Nuggets to hold onto Peyton Watson, who will be a restricted free agent at the end of the month.

 Julius Randle, Jaden McDaniels, Rudy Gobert, Mike Conley and Terrence Shannon Jr. will start against the Nuggets on Thursday. 
 With Dosunmu out, the Timberwolves find themselves in a tougher spot in Thursday’s closeout game. They’ll insert Shannon into the opening unit, who scored 15 points in Game 4. Minnesota will face a Denver team that is also dealing with a key injury to Aaron Gordon, who will not play in Game 6.

 Forward 
 #32 
 Aaron Gordon (calf) will not play against the Timberwolves on Thursday. 
 For the third time in this series, the Nuggets will be without their starting power forward. The versatile two-way forward has struggled with injuries throughout his 12th NBA season, and has played in only three of the five playoff games so far, averaging 11.3 points and 5.3 rebounds per game. Without Gordon, Spencer Jones should fill in again as the fifth starter. Jones scored 20 points and made four three-pointers in Denver’s Game 5 victory.

 Gordon did not play in Denver’s Game 5 victory on Monday, resulting in a move into the starting lineup for Spencer Jones. Shooting 4-of-5 from beyond the arc, Jones tallied 20 points, three steals and three blocked shots to help the Nuggets keep their season alive. He’ll get another start if Gordon remains out for another game.

 Gordon played 23 minutes in Saturday’s Game 4 loss to the Timberwolves before heading to the locker room in the third quarter. Despite the Nuggets saying he was available, Gordon didn’t return to the court. Now he’s been ruled out for Game 5. Expect Spencer Jones to start in his place.

 Aaron Gordon (calf) is questionable for Monday’s Game 5 against the Timberwolves. 
 Gordon, who played 23 minutes in Game 3, did not return after a third-quarter trip to the locker room despite the Nuggets saying that he was available. With the Nuggets’ backs against the wall, it would be unsurprising if he gave it a go on Monday. If Gordon can’t play, Spencer Jones is the most likely replacement in the starting lineup, but he offers little value on the offensive end. 
 Aaron Gordon 
 DEN

 Aaron Gordon (calf) recorded nine points (4-of-11 FGs), one rebound, one block and one three-pointer in Saturday’s Game 4 loss to the Timberwolves. 
 Back in action after a one-game absence, Gordon was placed in the starting lineup immediately. While he did play 23 minutes, the veteran forward did not appear to be himself. While the Nuggets said Gordon was available to return after a trip to the locker room during the third quarter, he did not. After the game, Nuggets head coach David Adelman said he believed it would be “unfair” to leave Gordon in. The Nuggets host Game 5 on Monday, and Spencer Jones (four rebounds, one steal and two blocks) may have to return to the starting lineup if Gordon can’t go.

 Kobe Sanders scored nine points (2-of-7 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs) with four rebounds, three steals and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers.
 With Rui Hachimura (quad) sidelined, the Clippers turned to Sanders to fill the void in the starting lineup. Beyond the steals, the production on Wednesday was limited. Sanders should only be rostered in extremely deep redraft leagues and dynasty leagues, even if Hachimura can’t play on Friday against the Timberwolves.

 Darius Garland finished Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers with 14 points (4-of-12 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), one rebound, five assists, one steal and one three-pointer.
 While Garland is shooting a respectable 46.3 percent from the field, turnovers have hurt his early-season value in nine-cat leagues. He committed five turnovers against the Lakers and is now averaging 5.8 per game. In four games, Garland has 26 assists and 23 turnovers. To be fair to Garland, he’s been playing through back tightness, according to Clippers head coach Tyronn Lue. And the hard fall he took on a layup attempt during the second half of Wednesday’s game didn’t help. Injuries have limited the Clippers’ rotation, and that may also explain Garland’s high turnover count. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Derrick Jones Jr. produced 15 points (6-of-10 FGs), five rebounds, four steals, two blocks and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers.
 Rostered in just 12 percent of Yahoo leagues, Jones is undervalued in category leagues. Against the Lakers, he recorded six “stocks” and shot 60 percent from the field. He’s now 10-of-18 from beyond the arc in four games. Will Jones sustain his current percentages from the field (57.6) and beyond the arc? Probably not. That said, he’s worth rostering while the Clippers await the returns of Brandon Ingram and Max Strus. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Keaton Wagler accounted for 21 points (4-of-15 FGs, 10-of-12 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers.
 A double-digit scorer in each of his first three regular-season games, Wagler finished Wednesday’s defeat with his first 20-point game. The rookie took advantage of the foul line against the Lakers, scoring 10 of his 21 points at the charity stripe. However, Wagler continues to struggle from the field, shooting 31.6 percent. The good news for fantasy managers is that he’s found other ways to provide value, making him a player worth rostering for those willing to take the field-goal percentage hit.

 Sandro Mamukelashvili tallied 13 points (6-of-15 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
 After totaling 21 points in the Lakers’ first three games, Mamukelashvili has hit double figures in each of his last two. Against the Clippers, his perimeter shot wasn’t falling, as he missed all five three-point attempts. But Mamu was 6-of-10 from two, and he did a little of everything else. Despite the bench role, Mamukelashvili is worth rostering in deep leagues.

 Quentin Grimes accumulated 23 points (7-of-15 FGs, 9-of-11 FTs), three rebounds, five assists and four steals in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
 Grimes replaced the injured Luka Dončić (back) in the starting lineup on Wednesday, and he was excellent. He led all scorers with 23 points and added some assists and steals. Grimes shot 0-of-3 from beyond the arc, but he was over 50 percent from two. Even in his usual reserve role, Grimes is worth rostering in deeper leagues because the Lakers need scorers beyond Dončić and Austin Reaves, and he can fill that role. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Kingston Flemings had 23 points (9-of-12 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers against the Heat on Wednesday. 
 Flemings came off the bench, played 28 minutes and had the best game of his young career so far. The 19-year-old rookie was impressive with 23 points on 12 attempts from the field and a full stat line. Flemings ended up playing more minutes than starter CJ McCollum, but don’t expect that to continue. Timing Flemings’ next outstanding performance will be difficult given his inconsistent playing time, making him more of a priority in dynasty formats. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Matisse Thybulle amassed 15 points (5-of-6 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), one rebound, two steals, one block and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
 Entering Wednesday, Thybulle was shooting 42.1 percent from three. His 4-of-5 night against the Clippers will increase that percentage, and fantasy managers can also benefit from the defensive stats. Given his play so far and the starting role, Thybulle should be rostered in deeper fantasy leagues.

 Austin Reaves accounted for 16 points (6-of-16 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, one assist, one steal and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
 The Lakers didn’t have Luka Dončić (back) on Wednesday, with his absence shifting Reaves into the starting point guard role. Unfortunately for fantasy managers hoping for more production from Reaves, it didn’t happen. More damaging than the field-goal percentage was the turnover count, as he racked up eight. The good news is that the Lakers play two more games in Week 2, starting with the Warriors on Friday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Collin Sexton finished Wednesday’s win over the Clippers with 21 points (6-of-11 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and four three-pointers.
 In his first three games this season, Sexton totaled 27 points on 11-of-28 shooting from the field. With Luka Dončić (back) out, Sexton didn’t move into the starting lineup, but his playmaking role off the bench became even more important on Wednesday. The veteran guard shot over 50 percent from the field overall and 4-of-7 from three in his best performance of the season to date. While he hasn’t been consistent enough to merit a roster spot in 12-team leagues, Sexton is worth considering in deeper leagues. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson
